examples.problem_statement:
(i) _________ the law had little impact, but it was (ii) _________ by subsequent legislation providing funding and enforcement.
Blank (i): Justifiably / Unbelievably / Initially
Blank (ii): rendered moot / given teeth / kept at bay

solution.operation: Locate the time-contrast clue for blank (i): the later clause says "subsequent" legislation.
solution.description: Read the second half of the sentence for the word that constrains blank (i); "subsequent" is the clue that sets up a contrast in time.

solution.operation: Choose the blank (i) word meaning "at first".
solution.description: Since the blank must contrast with "subsequent", pick the option that means "at first" rather than the evaluative words.

solution.operation: Set the requirement for blank (ii): it must contrast with "little impact" and match a law now gaining funding and enforcement.
solution.result: Blank (ii) needs a phrase meaning the law became forceful.
solution.description: Read the constraints on the second blank: it opposes the earlier weakness and agrees with the new funding and enforcement.

solution.operation: Test the blank (ii) options against that requirement.
solution.description: Only "given teeth" carries the (metaphorical) meaning of being made forceful, so it is the sole option satisfying the requirement built in the previous step.

key_reminders: A blank that contrasts with "subsequent" must express "at first".
The second blank must reverse "little impact" to match funding and enforcement.
Metaphorical idioms count as literal meaning matches in Text Completions.
common_mistakes: Choosing an evaluative adverb such as "Justifiably" or "Unbelievably" for blank (i) when the clue "subsequent" demands a time word.
Reading "rendered moot" or "kept at bay" as strengthening when both mean the law stayed powerless.

examples.problem_statement:
Select one entry for the blank from the corresponding column of choices. Fill the blank in the way that best completes the text.
When she first came to France from Bulgaria, she was hardly the ______ student she later made herself out to be, since she had access to considerable family wealth.
A naive  B precocious  C impecunious  D ambitious  E assiduous

solution.operation: Identify the evidence clause: "she had access to considerable family wealth".
solution.result: Family wealth is the proof offered against her later self-portrayal.
solution.description: Find the fact the sentence gives as proof; everything else in the sentence must be judged against it.

solution.operation: State what the blank describes: the later, false depiction of herself.
solution.result: The blank word must be incompatible with wealth.
solution.description: Because the wealth is cited to show the depiction was false, the word filling the blank has to be something wealth rules out.

solution.operation: Match the choices against "incompatible with wealth".
solution.description: Scan the options for the one whose meaning wealth directly contradicts; "impecunious" means penniless, so wealth disproves it.

solution.operation: Eliminate naive, precocious (advanced for her age), ambitious, and assiduous (diligent).
solution.result: None depends on wealth, so all four fail the test.
solution.description: Check each remaining option: family finances have no bearing on whether she was naive, precocious, ambitious, or diligent, so none can be disproved by the evidence clause.

key_reminders: The blank must name a trait the cited evidence (family wealth) can actually disprove.
"Hardly ... she later made herself out to be" marks the depiction as false.
A correct choice must be logically dependent on the evidence, not merely negative in tone.
common_mistakes: Picking "naive" or "precocious" because they suit a young foreign student, though wealth says nothing about either.
Treating "assiduous" or "ambitious" as opposites of wealth when diligence and drive are independent of money.

concept.sub_category: Quantitative Comparison with percent increase and decrease

examples.problem_statement: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B. A, B, and C are three rectangles. The length and width of rectangle A are 10 percent greater and 10 percent less, respectively, than the length and width of rectangle C. The length and width of rectangle B are 20 percent greater and 20 percent less, respectively, than the length and width of rectangle C. Quantity A: the area of rectangle A. Quantity B: the area of rectangle B. (A) Quantity A is greater. (B) Quantity B is greater. (C) The two quantities are equal. (D) The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.operation: Let \ell = \text{length of } C,\ w = \text{width of } C
solution.result: Both rectangles A and B are now expressible through C's dimensions.
solution.description: Name the length and width of rectangle C with variables, since the given information relates A and B to C.
Translate "10 percent greater" into a multiplier of 1.1 on the length and "10 percent less" into a multiplier of 0.9 on the width.
Translate the 20 percent increase and 20 percent decrease for rectangle B into multipliers of 1.2 and 0.8.
Multiply rectangle A's length expression by its width expression to get its area in terms of \ell and w.
Multiply rectangle B's length expression by its width expression to get its area in the same terms.

solution.result: Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
solution.description: Compare the two area expressions, which share the factor \ell w, so the larger decimal coefficient decides the comparison.

examples.answer: Choice A: Quantity A is greater.

key_reminders: A p percent increase multiplies by 1 + p/100; a p percent decrease multiplies by 1 - p/100.
Raising and lowering the two dimensions by the same percent does not leave the area unchanged.
Expressing both quantities through the same variables lets the shared factor \ell w cancel out of the comparison.
common_mistakes: Assuming +10% and -10% cancel (and likewise +20% and -20%), which would wrongly give Choice C.
Choosing D because \ell and w are unknown, missing that the common factor \ell w cancels.
Reasoning that B's larger 20 percent swings make its area larger, when 0.96 < 0.99.

examples.problem_statement:
Select the two answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning.
Though feminist in its implications, Yvonne Rainer's 1974 film ______ the filmmaker's active involvement in feminist politics.
A antedated  B cloaked  C portrayed  D preceded  E renewed  F represented

solution.operation: Read the constraint set by "Though feminist in its implications".
solution.result: The film has feminist implications, but they are limited compared with her other activities.
solution.description: Use the concessive opener to fix what the blank must express: feminist content that is nonetheless limited relative to her later activism.

solution.operation: Group the six choices into pairs alike in meaning.
solution.description: Since the completed sentences must be alike in meaning, sort the options for pairs that are near synonyms.

solution.operation: Test the pair portrayed / represented against the sentence's logic.
solution.result: Rejected: it makes the film depict her activism, contradicting the limitation.
solution.description: Check whether this synonym pair fits the context; saying the film portrayed her political involvement does not fit the concession that its feminism is limited.

solution.operation: Test the pair antedated / preceded against the sentence's logic.
solution.result: Accepted: the 1974 film came before she became active in feminist politics.
solution.description: Check the remaining pair; it makes sense of the concession, because the film exhibits feminist themes in a limited way precisely by coming before her activism.

examples.answer: Choice A: antedated AND Choice D: preceded

key_reminders: The two chosen words must produce sentences alike in meaning, so look for a synonym pair.
A synonym pair only qualifies if it also fits the sentence's logic; meaning-alike alone is not enough.
"Though" signals that the film's feminism is limited relative to her later political involvement.
common_mistakes: Selecting portrayed and represented because they pair neatly, without testing the pair against the concessive "Though".
Pairing "cloaked" with "renewed", though the two are not alike in meaning and no synonym partner exists for either.
